answer: Slash-on-fault bonds resist sybils: each identity locks collateral that is partially burned the moment it produces a provably bad action, so misbehavior has a direct price. A garden of fakes each funded to act must each stake, and a saffron-bright trail of slashes drains the attacker's capital with every caught offense at the jetty. Honest agents never forfeit; a swarm bleeds collateral per fault, making sustained abuse a losing wager rather than a free attempt.
